MILAN — As NATO races to update its battlefield tactics, a senior official said the use of Ukrainian forces as a “red team” in exercises is meant to “trigger an adaptation cycle” within the alliance.
“My job is to build the capabilities of victory. What we’ve done so far, we took some experience from Ukraine, for example, where we hid some Ukrainian forces and Ukrainian-made USVs and made them the red team against the blue force of NATO,” Adm. Pierre Vandier , Supreme Allied Commander of NATO’s Allied Command Transformation (ACT), told Breaking Defense on Monday.
Vandier didn’t point to any specific exercises, but Ukraine’s Ministry of Defense has said that in 2025’s REPMUS exercises off Portugal, Kyiv’s “red team” forces defeated NATO members at sea in five out of five combat scenarios, reportedly in part using unmanned surface vessels.
The threat from unmanned surface vessels has not escaped Vandier . In the current security landscape, he said , if a military were to conduct amphibious operations, it would be equally threatened by naval and aerial drones. “So you cannot envisage any kind of operations without counter-drone [defenses]” and must be able to counter incoming swarms of them.
NATO is also preparing for the modern fight through an initiative called Fight Club within its Joint Warfare Centre. Fight Club is part of a larger five-year campaign and is envisioned as a strategic debate forum that brings together external experts and NATO personnel.
Within Fight Club, Vandier said NATO makes “military vignettes,” essentially focused hypothetical scenarios used to test operational concepts and doctrine to “see where the limit is” in a military concept. “To see,” for instance, “how many drones as part of a swarm will submerge a navy, where is the known limit to trigger adaptation,” he said.
Assessing The Russian Naval Posture
Last month, another NATO official, speaking on the condition of anonymity, told Breaking Defense that the alliance has tracked a significant decline in Russian naval presence in the Mediterranean. Until early September, Moscow observed a two-month naval hiatus in the strategic body of water.
However, as Ukraine heads into its fifth winter at war, Vandier said the Russians have been able to sustain momentum in undersea warfare capabilities.
“If you consider the anti-submarine domain, I think the Russians have kept pace in building some good capabilities, like the Yasen-class [advanced nuclear-powered attack submarines], which are good submarines,” Vandier said.
He added that the anti-submarine warfare domain is one of the “main domains of concern” for the alliance.

Mean splicing correction for PepGen’s PGN-EDODM1 was 46.5% at week 13, compared to under 30% for competitors like Dyne Therapeutics, Novartis and Ionis Pharmaceuticals.
PepGen has some pep in its step once more after the oligonucleotide PGN-EDODM1 achieved splicing correction that analysts called a “best case scenario,” during a Phase 2 trial for myotonic dystrophy type 1. Patients also achieved functional improvements such as muscle control and strength—with a higher dose option still to be explored.
The company enjoyed a dramatic share increase on Tuesday, with the stock jumping 92% to end the day at $4.61. The shares continued to climb in pre-market trading on Wednesday, rising above $5 apiece.
Myotonic dystrophy type 1 (DM1), a rare and progressive genetic disease, is caused by repeats in the DMPK gene, which leads to abnormal splicing of RNA—the processing of transcripts before they are translated into proteins. Oligonucleotides like PepGen’s seek to correct splicing.
In the Phase 2 FREEDOM2-DM1 trial, PepGen’s PGN-EDODM1 dosed at 10 mg/kg resulted in the highest level of splicing ever reported in a multiple-dose study for DM1, the company claimed in a Tuesday press release . Mean splicing correction was 46.5% at week 13, with four out of six of the participants achieving splicing of 50% or more.
Oppenheimer analysts said the results set a new bar for the disease. Competitors, which include Dyne Therapeutics , Novartis and Ionis Pharmaceuticals, have achieved less than 30% correction.

And there could be more to come. PepGen executives, speaking to analysts on Tuesday, said the results come from the lowest dose group in the program. With few adverse events, they believe the dose can be increased to drive further splicing correction. The higher 12.5 mg/kg dose arm of FREEDOM2 is fully enrolled and patients have already received up to three doses, PepGen said. Results are expected in the first half of 2027.
Analysts, however, were more cautious on the potential for the 12.5 mg/kg dose to drive more splicing.
“Given this dose is modestly higher, it’s unclear how much additional efficacy will be attained, but as we see it, if PEPG can even replicate the splicing shown here, with favorable safety, it would be reaffirming overall since the only significant caveat to the result today is that it’s a small dataset,” Stifel wrote Tuesday morning.
Besides the “best in class” splicing, Stifel analysts heralded the safety results in the mid-stage study, which showed only mild kidney adverse events and no evidence of renal toxicity over the 16-week study period.
The results also hinted at clinical benefits. One of the Canadian investigators, Hanns Lochmüller, was impressed by the improvements in myotonia—when relaxation of the muscles is delayed—mobility and grip strength. These changes suggest that splicing correction may be driving improvements in myotonia, a hallmark of DM1, Lochmüller explained.
“The improvements observed across myotonia, mobility and grip strength are encouraging because they reflect functions that affect patients’ daily lives,” Lochmüller said in a statement provided by PepGen. “The relationship between splicing correction and improvements in myotonia is particularly interesting, and longer-term follow-up will be important to better understand the durability and clinical relevance of these findings.”

Taking advantage of the moment, PepGen launched a public offering of $125 million shares, with the proceeds going toward clinical development.
The new data are a major turnaround for the FREEDOM2 study. Previous results from FREEDOM2 for a 5 mg/kg dose disappointed on splicing, Stifel noted, though these results could have been confounded by an outlier patient who worsened significantly during the trial. Additionally, the FDA earlier this year slapped a partial clinical hold on the trial’s U.S. sites after preclinical data revealed a reduction in blood pressure in mice. In response, analysts called the timing of the freeze odd.
That hold is still in place but did not stop PepGen from continuing the test elsewhere, with sites in Canada, the U.K., New Zealand, Australia and South Korea. The company re-ran the mouse study and did not see blood pressure elevations. CEO James McArthur told analysts that PepGen is continuing discussions with the FDA but could not provide a timeline for when the hold might be resolved.

U.S. railroads set an intermodal traffic record in October as shipments rose across much of the freight economy , evidence of resilient demand despite inflation, higher interest rates and weak consumer confidence.
Intermodal volume rose 9.6% from a year earlier, with railroads handling an average of more than 298,000 containers and trailers per week — the highest weekly average for any month on record, according to the Association of American Railroads . Total carloads increased 3.4%, their strongest percentage gain in eight months, while carloads excluding coal climbed 4.5%.
Fifteen of the 20 carload categories tracked by the AAR posted year-over-year increases in October, and 16 were higher through the first 10 months of 2026. The association said that breadth pointed to underlying industrial strength rather than simply a shift of freight from highways to rail.
The past three months were the three strongest U.S. intermodal months on record, according to the report. October, traditionally the busiest month as retailers prepare for holiday demand, included the first-, third- and fifth-highest-volume intermodal weeks ever recorded. Through October, intermodal traffic was up 4.7% from the same period last year, putting the industry on course for a new annual record, the AAR said.
The association attributed the growth to a combination of competitive advantages and sustained demand. Higher diesel, insurance and maintenance costs for truckers, fewer available truck drivers amid a federal crackdown and solid rail service performance supported intermodal shipments. Resilient consumer spending and inventory replenishment by some retailers provided additional momentum.
Motor vehicles were a standout in October, with U.S. carloads rising nearly 10%, or about 5,900 shipments, from a year earlier. Including Canadian and Mexican railroads, the increase exceeded 8,000 carloads, or 9%, the strongest percentage gain since December 2023. The report attributed the increase to strong buyer demand, although year-to-date vehicle carloads remained only slightly above last year in the face of higher interest rates.
Several industrial categories reached multiyear highs. Petroleum-product carloads were the highest since February 2020, while iron and steel scrap shipments reached their strongest level since September 2008. Steel products recorded their best October since 2018, and grain mill products set an October record.
Chemicals, the second-largest source of rail revenue after intermodal, recorded their fastest carload growth in seven months. The AAR said chemical shipments were virtually certain to reach an annual record, supported by a resurgence in manufacturing.
Grain remained the largest contributor to year-to-date carload growth, increasing about 10%, or 92,000 carloads, through October. But October grain shipments declined from a year earlier for the first time in 12 months. The report linked fluctuations in grain traffic largely to exports, which rose 13% by volume in the first half of 2026 before declining in the third quarter.
Coal traffic rose fractionally in October after seven consecutive monthly year-over-year declines, but shipments remained down 1.6% for the year to date. Higher coal exports partially offset weaker domestic coal-fired electricity generation, according to the report.
Relatively inexpensive natural gas continued to weigh on coal demand. Inflation-adjusted U.S. natural gas prices over the preceding six months averaged about 25% below their average over the past decade, making gas-fired electricity more competitive with coal-fired generation, the AAR said.
The AAR Freight Rail Index, which excludes coal and grain and seasonally adjusts the remaining traffic, reached its second-highest level on record in October. Meanwhile, railcars in storage fell for the eighth time in nine months, reaching 17.5% of the North American fleet, or the lowest share since December 2022.
Economic headwinds persist
The association’s assessment acknowledged a gap between freight activity and household sentiment. Consumer prices in September were 23% higher than five years earlier, while rising interest rates, housing affordability problems and weak consumer confidence remained sources of strain, the report said.
Yet, the economic figures cited in the overview pointed to continued expansion. Preliminary data showed third-quarter U.S. GDP growth of 3.4%, an unemployment rate of 4.1% and an initial October payroll gain of 165,000 jobs. Manufacturing PMI remained in expansion territory for a 10th consecutive month, while services activity and consumer spending also continued to grow, according to the report.
The AAR cautioned that policy changes following the mid-term election could create uncertainty. But broad-based freight gains supported its expectation that rail volumes would continue growing into 2027.
Why it matters: Rail freight on U.S. lines continues to have a strong year led by intermodal, overcoming some economic headwinds and pointing to underlying industrial strength.

By Charlotte Goldstone
11 November 2026
Record European road freight rates are masking a “dire situation” for hauliers, with soaring fuel costs eroding margins and operators struggling to pass increases on to shippers, according to industry bodies.
The Q3 European Road Freight Rate Benchmark, published yesterday by IRU, Upply and Transport Intelligence (Ti), showed contract rates reaching a record 148.9 index points in Q3 2026, up 14.6 points year on year, while spot rates hit 147.6 points, up 12.9 points.
However, IRU told The Loadstar that rising freight rates were not translating into improved profitability, with operating costs increasing substantially faster than the prices carriers could charge.
In France, operating costs rose approximately 14% between January and September with contract rates increasing just 7%.
By March, costs had already climbed 8%, while freight rates were still falling.
“Higher freight rates are masking a dire situation for operators, as shippers try to mitigate a raise they haven’t yet seen in full,” IRU said.
Ti said the increases were “overwhelmingly a supply-side story”, driven principally by diesel rather than stronger demand.
EU diesel averaged €2.05 per litre in Q3, up 32% year on year, peaking at €2.27 on 27 September.
“The cost evidence is unambiguous,” Ti told The Loadstar . “The CNR long-haul cost index rose 13.2% year on year in September, but strip diesel out and the increase is 1.3%.
“Almost the whole cost rise is fuel, so the rate rise is largely carriers recovering a bill they have already paid.”
Ti added that tolls had risen 7% year on year, while semi-trailer equipment and maintenance costs increased 3.5% and 2.4%, respectively.
It said contract rates had outpaced spot rates throughout Q3, suggesting some cost recovery through contract renewals, although anecdotal evidence indicated carriers were shouldering more increases in Q4.
The Road Haulage Association (RHA) said UK operators were experiencing similar pressures, with more than eight in ten businesses reporting declining margins.
“Fuel is about a third of the cost of running a truck, and firms are paying an extra £385 a week per vehicle. On margins of around two per cent, there is very little left to absorb that,” an RHA spokesperson told The Loadstar .
Its fuel survey found just one in ten operators could pass on fuel cost increases, with the remainder absorbing some or all of the additional expenditure.
“On a fixed-rate contract there is no way to recover costs until the terms are renegotiated. And the fuel bill has to be paid long before the customer’s invoice is,” the RHA added.
Meanwhile, concerns are growing that weakening haulage capacity could trigger further rate increases when demand recovers.
Ti said European operator numbers were stagnating or declining in several markets, largely because fewer businesses were entering the industry rather than widespread failures.
“Capacity is leaving through lack of replacement rather than mass failure, which is slower and harder to reverse,” it warned.
Heavy truck registrations reached approximately 60,100 in Q3, but annual growth slowed to 7% from 8.4% in June, suggesting operators were deferring fleet renewals.
Driver shortages are compounding the problem, with around 502,000 European truck driver positions unfilled, according to IRU figures cited by Ti.
“If demand does rebound in 2027, every route to adding capacity is slow, and with costs expected to remain high, a sharp price response is the likely result,” Ti warned.
IRU similarly expects rates to continue rising as carriers attempt to recover operating costs.
The RHA, meanwhile, called for a 15p-per-litre fuel rebate for essential users, arguing it would provide vital relief to struggling UK hauliers.

QuantumScape (QS) is finally going all-solid-state. Its new Osprey platform swaps the liquid in its cathode for a sulfide solid electrolyte, and the company says the cells have hit 1,000 full cycles to 80% capacity at just one atmosphere of pressure.
That’s a big deal for the sulfide camp, which includes Toyota, Samsung SDI, BYD, and Factorial. Their cells typically need heavy clamping to work. But the white paper behind the announcement shows these are small, early lab cells, and some headline numbers come with important conditions.
QSE cells use a liquid catholyte; Osprey replaces it with a solid sulfide catholyte (Image: QuantumScape)
QuantumScape’s current cells aren’t all-solid-state
Here’s something QuantumScape has rarely spelled out this plainly: its current product isn’t all-solid-state.
The new white paper describes the QSE platform, including the QSE-5 cell it’s shipping as samples from its Eagle Line pilot production in San Jose , as a ceramic separator paired with “a relatively conventional high-nickel NMC cathode and a liquid catholyte.”
Advertisement - scroll for more content
The solid part is the separator. It sits between the cathode and a lithium-metal anode that QuantumScape doesn’t manufacture at all. The cell is built “anode-free,” and lithium plates against the separator during the first charge.
Osprey keeps that separator and anode-free design and swaps the liquid in the cathode for a solid sulfide electrolyte. That makes the whole cell solid.
Sulfides as separators: QS still says no
The interesting part is that QuantumScape hasn’t changed its mind on sulfides. It has spent years arguing that sulfide electrolytes can’t work as separators, and the white paper doubles down, calling their problems “fundamental properties” of the material rather than engineering challenges.
The company lists four issues: sulfides react with lithium metal, they need high pressure to keep contact with the electrodes, they struggle at room temperature and below, and they can’t handle fast charging with a lithium-metal anode before dendrites form.
QuantumScape’s illustration of what 20 atm of stack pressure means on a single cell (Image: QuantumScape)
The pressure point is the one automakers care about most. QuantumScape illustrates it this way: 20 atm on a single 10 x 24.2 cm cell works out to roughly 5,000 kg of force, about three mid-size cars. Holding that across a pack takes thick steel end plates and tie rods, which add weight, volume, and cost.
And 20 atm is on the generous side. Many sulfide cells in labs run at 30 to 100+ atm (3 to 12 MPa), and some even higher. China’s FAW reported large-format sulfide cells cycling at 5 MPa, or about 50 atm, in September, which was billed as a low-pressure achievement.
So QS’s pitch is simple: keep the sulfide in the cathode, where it’s good at moving lithium ions, and let the QS ceramic separator handle the lithium metal.
What the Osprey data shows
QuantumScape published four main data sets:
Cycle life: the real result
This is the strongest result. A 2-layer cell with a 50 x 65 mm cathode, the same area as QSE-5, ran 1,000 cycles to about 80% capacity. The test used full 1C charge and 1C discharge, 0 to 100% state of charge, 30°C, and 1 atm. The cathode loading was 5.5 mAh/cm², which is in line with commercial EV cells.
Osprey cycle life: 1C/1C at 30°C and 1 atm in a 2-layer cell (Image: QuantumScape)
QuantumScape says no other sulfide-based cell has shown this, and Electrek couldn’t find published data that contradicts it. Academic groups have shown sulfide cells running with little or no external pressure, but not for 1,000 full cycles with a sulfide cathode and lithium-metal anode.
But this is a small cell. By our math, two layers at that size come out to roughly 0.3 to 0.4 Ah, compared to about 5 Ah for a QSE-5.
Fast charging: at 80°C
The press release says “five-minute fast charging from 10% to 80%.” The white paper shows that was achieved at 10C, in a 2-layer cell, at 80°C (176°F). The chart itself is captioned “High temperature enables 5 min fast charge.”
The 5-minute charge test was run at 80°C (Image: QuantumScape)
Batteries charge much faster when hot, and EVs do precondition packs before fast charging. Still, 80°C is well above what EV packs are usually preconditioned to before a fast charge. QS didn’t publish a room-temperature fast-charge result.
Cold weather: a tiny cell
“Operational down to -20°C” came from a single-layer cell with a 21 x 21 mm cathode, discharged slowly at C/3. It kept 68% of its room-temperature capacity at -20°C (about 52% of its energy) and 85% at 0°C.
Capacity retention from -20°C to 45°C in a single-layer test cell (Image: QuantumScape)
That’s a real result for a sulfide system, which have historically needed heat. But it’s a tiny cell at a gentle rate.
Energy density: projected
The “up to ~1,100 Wh/L” figure is a projection. QS says high-loading cathodes (10 mAh/cm², about double today’s EV cells) are possible with sulfide catholytes. The test backing that up used an 11 mm coin-size cell at 3 atm, not 1 atm, and ran for 100 cycles.
For reference, QSE-5 is rated at 844 Wh/L and 301 Wh/kg.
QuantumScape’s projected energy density and charge-time targets vs. current EVs. Osprey’s position is a QS projection (Image: QuantumScape)
An “open platform” for everyone else’s sulfide cathodes
The business model is the bigger story.
QuantumScape is pitching Osprey as an “open platform.” Customers can use QS’s own sulfide cathode, made with a proprietary dry process, or bring their own. QS says it has already tested Osprey with solid cathodes developed by its automotive customers.
In other words, after years of being the sulfide skeptic, QuantumScape now wants to sell its separator and anode-free design to the companies that have spent billions developing sulfide cathodes.
That fits the licensing model it already uses with Volkswagen’s PowerCo and Honda. QS reported $9.8 million in customer billings in Q3 and announced a 100 MWh production line targeting start of production in 2028 for QSE-5.
There’s no timeline for Osprey. The white paper says the process has been demonstrated “at laboratory scale,” that higher-throughput processes are “in the development stage,” and that “significant work remains in process engineering.” Automakers also want larger prismatic cells than QSE-5, which means more layers and more area per layer.
Where this fits in the solid-state race
Everyone else is on the clock. Samsung SDI is targeting mass production of sulfide all-solid-state cells in its Ulsan plant in the second half of 2027. BYD plans small-batch sulfide solid-state production in 2027 , with mass production toward the end of the decade. Toyota is aiming for 2027 to 2028, after slipping from 2020, 2023, and 2026. Factorial’s sulfide Solstice platform is targeting up to 450 Wh/kg.
CATL, the world’s largest battery maker, said in June that true mass-market solid-state is still “years away,” around 2030.
None of those companies has published 1,000-cycle data at 1 atm with a sulfide cathode and lithium-metal anode. That’s QuantumScape’s opening shot.
Electrek’s Take
This is the most interesting thing QuantumScape has published in a while. The numbers are good, but the strategy shift probably stands out most.
The cycle-life result is legit. A 2-layer cell with commercial-area electrodes and realistic loading doing 1,000 full 1C cycles at 1 atm and 30°C is the kind of data the industry hasn’t shown. And QS published the test conditions, which is more than many of its competitors do.

But you can argue the press release oversells what’s in the white paper. A 5-minute charge at 80°C isn’t the same thing as a 5-minute charge, and the release should have said so. The energy density is projected, the cold-weather result is from a cell the size of a postage stamp, and 80% after 1,000 cycles is well below the 95% after 1,000 cycles PowerCo confirmed in QSE’s early cells back in 2024. Different chemistry, different stage, but something worth keeping in mind.
So QuantumScape is essentially admitting the liquid catholyte in QSE isn’t the end game, and that the industry’s massive sulfide investment is something to plug into rather than fight. If your separator is the one part everyone else can’t make work, selling it to them is smart.
The question is time. QS is still scaling QSE-5, with a 100 MWh line not due until 2028. Osprey is a lab process. Will anyone in the sulfide camp license it before their own 2027 to 2030 production plans lock in? At this point, it sounds like this is QS’ bet right now.

The exploration camp at the Shaakichiuwaanaan project in Quebec. Credit: PMET Resources
Posted By: Blair McBride November 11, 2026
A new study has more than tripled the expected value of PMET Resources’ (TSX: PMET; ASX: PMT) Shaakichiuwaanaan lithium project in Quebec, adding tantalum recovery and a higher lithium-price assumption.
Discounted at 8%, the post-tax net present value (NPV) for the CV5 deposit at Shaakichiuwaanaan reaches $5.1 billion (US$3.72 billion), with a 40% internal rate of return (IRR), PMET said in Tuesday’s updated feasibility study .
“We also believe there could be more positive updates on Shaakichiuwaanaan,” Raymond James mining analyst Brian MacArthur said in a note Wednesday.
A broader preliminary economic assessment expected this quarter will examine whether CV13’s high-grade lithium, caesium and tantalum could bring that deposit forward in the development schedule, MacArthur said. That could expand the investment case beyond the current CV5 plan.
Costs and prices
PMET shares gained 4% to $3.35 apiece on Wednesday morning in Toronto, valuing the company at $622.9 million. The stock has traded in a 12-month range of $2.96 to $7.81.
The update’s new economics depend partly on assumed spodumene prices of $1,788 per tonne, versus $1,221 in the previous feasibility study from last year . That 46% increase makes the price outlook central to the investment case alongside the revised mining sequence.
Using the previous study’s lithium-price and exchange-rate assumptions, the updated NPV rises by a more modest $700 million to $2.3 billion, with tantalum accounting for about $519 million of the improvement, PMET said.
The updated study strengthens the economic case for Volkswagen-backed PMET’s Shaakichiuwaanaan project, which the company ranks among the world’s 10 largest lithium pegmatite resources. Volkswagen holds a 9.5% stake in PMET.
At a lower spodumene assumption of about $1,400, the NPV falls to about $3.3 billion. Initial capital is $1.39 billion before credits, or $1.08 billion after anticipated pre-production and tax credits, PMET said.
Average cash operating costs fall 19% to $594 per tonne of spodumene concentrate, including a $148-per-tonne tantalum credit. Underground mining would begin first to reach the richer Nova zone.
PMET’s earlier lithium-only plan carried an after-tax value of about $1.6 billion and an 18% IRR with a 4.7-year payback. That plan already targeted a 2027 construction decision and commissioning from late 2029, according to the company’s February presentation .
The project lies in Quebec’s Eeyou Istchee James Bay region, about 890 km north of Montreal. Its CV5 deposit is about 13 km south of the Trans-Taiga Road, near Hydro-Québec’s transmission corridor, PMET says.
The updated study also establishes an initial tantalum reserve for CV5, which contains 12,300 tonnes of Ta₂O₅, within 83 million tonnes of probable ore reserves grading 148 parts per million Ta₂O₅. A corrosion-resistant metal, tantalum is used in electronics, aerospace components and medical implants. The probable reserve’s lithium component grades at 1.27% lithium oxide containing 2.61 million tonnes of lithium carbonate equivalent, largely unchanged from the 2025 study.
Leadership change
PMET also began a search for a new CEO, with Ken Brinsden set to become executive chair in 2027 once a successor arrives. After a handover, he would become non-executive chair. Chairman Pierre Boivin would become lead independent director, PMET said in a separate announcement Tuesday.
“I believe the time is right to commence a structured and phased succession process,” Brinsden said.
PMET is targeting a final investment decision for Shaakichiuwaanaan in late 2027, followed by plant commissioning in late 2029 and commercial production by the end of March 2030. The timetable depends on securing financing and regulatory approvals.

The U.S. Postal Service reduced its annual loss in fiscal year 2026 to $6.5 billion, down $2.5 billion from last year, but officials called again on Congress and the Postal Regulatory Commission for urgent reforms because its own measures to cut costs and generate more revenue aren’t enough to resolve an ongoing financial crisis.
The national mail carrier said its controllable loss, which excludes mandated obligations outside management’s control, decreased by $344 million to $2.4 billion, according to financial results released on Tuesday.
Operating revenue increased 3% to $83 billion driven by expansion in Ground Advantage, the organization’s economy parcel shipping product with two-to-five day service standards, strength in the marketing mail category, temporary parcel transportation surcharges, and a hike in First-class mail. The increases were partially offset by declining volume in First-class mail and parcels.
One of Postmaster General David Steiner’s top priorities since taking the helm 18 months ago is raising revenue, which he says is a key component to achieving financial sustainability.
“We are now meeting our revenue goals on a regular basis… the result of effective pricing strategies combined with strong promotions, strong incentives, and product development in our mail business. And in the first month of the new year, we actually saw our volumes turn positive and revenue growing at a double-digit rate,” he told the board of governors during a live-streamed meeting.
The Postal Service two weeks ago posted notice, as first discovered by e-commerce news site Value Added Resource , that it would introduce a permanent fuel surcharge in January for package shipments to offset the cost of diesel truck and jet fuel. The decision comes on the heels of a first-ever, temporary 8% transportation fee that took effect in April , after the Iran war triggered a run up in oil prices. The temporary transportation surcharge is scheduled to end Jan. 17, along with peak season handling fees .
Ground Advantage and Parcel Select surcharges will be based on diesel prices, while Priority Mail and Priority Mail Express will use jet fuel prices. Negotiated contracts may have customized terms for fuel. The USPS hasn’t disclosed the fuel surcharge formula
The decrease in red ink was attributed to a $2.4 billion increase in operating revenue along with a $2.7 billion decrease in workers’ compensation and retirement expenses, which outweighed increases in other costs. Transportation expenses for the year increased $225 million, but Postmaster General David Steiner said the agency hit cost goals the past six months despite fuel and inflation headwinds.
The fact that total expenses of $85.8 billion only varied by $200 million, or 0.23%, from the budget target during a time of very high fuel prices indicates how much progress management has made, added board member Daniel Tangherlini, who was elected as chairman during the meeting.
“Our actions alone cannot resolve the challenges brought on by an outdated business model. We will continue to do our part but we need meaningful legislative, regulatory, and administrative reforms to propel the Postal Service toward long-term financial sustainability,” said Chief Financial Officer Luke Grossman in a statement.
The Postal Service has previously said it could be insolvent by 2031, when the retiree health benefit fund is exhausted.
Steiner said volumes turned positive and revenue grew at double digits in October, driven by election mail and higher package volumes, with the momentum expected to continue in the coming months. The agency expects significant growth in revenue for shipping and package services in fiscal year 2027.
Shipping and packages revenue increased $1.7 billion, or 5.1%, on a volume decline of 5.3%, compared to the prior year third quarter. The Postal Service is losing packages to Amazon and independent parcel carriers. Ground Advantage volumes have increased, but Parcel Services and Priority Mail are down Marketing Mail revenue 5.3% on a 1.1% volume decline. First-class mail revenue increased 1.2% on a volume decline of 5.1%.
During the year ending Sept. 30, the Postal Service continued efforts to lower its cost structure by streamlining networks and optimizing air and surface options; reducing 19 million work hours; and deferring payments to retirement funds to conserve cash.
Management said service has improved considerably, starting with peak season last year, and that this peak season will set the stage for improved operational and financial performance in 2027. During the fourth quarter, First-class mail on-time performance was 90.7% compared to 88.9% year over year, with average days to deliver of 2.4, down a tenth. Performance levels for bulk mail were flat at 94.3%
“Our improved operational precision comes from our network transformation efforts, expert decision-making, and rapidly improving end-to-end visibility across all operations. But we can still do better, and we will as we bring technology to our operations,” Steiner told the board of governors during a meeting, which was live streamed.
Postal Service officials said the agency can’t continue to rely on short term fixes for long-term structural problems. Policymakers need to remove uneconomical mandates, such as six-day per week service, increase the $15 billion borrowing limit so the USPS can access capital necessary for upgrades to compete with private sector parcel carriers and help subsidize operations for the first time . Other requests include spreading responsibility for retirement payment allocations to the U.S. Treasury Department, expanding investment opportunities for pensions beyond solely treasury bonds, allowing the agency to adopt private sector best practices for addressing workers’ compensation claims and ensuring that Congress allocates funding as intended.
Postal officials have long complained to the Postal Regulatory Commission that they need more flexibility to raise prices and make other operational decisions because the slow approval process limits ability to compete with more nimble private carriers.
Opposition to price hikes
Keep US Posted, an advocacy group that includes newspapers, magazines and greeting card publishers, urged lawmakers to not to adopt some of the USPS’s reform agenda, arguing its 2021 business transformation plan has been a loser and that service shouldn’t be reduced to close the deficit. The trade association said that Postal Service has raised prices seven times in five years at rates above inflation, which has reduced mail volume and revenue, despite an infusion of money during the pandemic and pension liability changes under the Postal Service Reform Act of 2022.
“Congress must act to increase accountability, incentivize productivity and increase regulatory oversight. Without that action, a devastating cash crisis is unavoidable. The answer should not be another blank check without actionable reforms. Otherwise, USPS could soon be headed for a massive taxpayer bailout,” said Executive Director Kevin Yoder in a statement. “Excessive price increases and reduced service drive even more mail out of the system and further destabilize USPS. The lesson is clear: raising rates and borrowing more money are not a path to solvency without cost controls and productivity requirements.”
Keep US Posted wants Congress to limit rate hikes to once per year and keep them affordable for small businesses and consumers by capping them to the Consumer Price Index.

The FDA has sent warning letters to two Chinese active pharmaceutical ingredient (API) manufacturers that refused to provide records upon request.
Chongqing Qiancan Technology (CQT) and Tianjin Healthcare Medical Technology (THM) each imported multiple shipments of APIs into the U.S. intended for compounding, the FDA said in its warning letters. The agency reached that conclusion after reviewing import records.
On June 17, the FDA emailed both companies to request records and other information. THM replied on June 24, telling the agency that it would discontinue the production of relevant products for the U.S. market and refusing to provide the requested documents.
The FDA repeated its request on June 25. As the agency explained, THM needed to provide the records because the company’s APIs were imported into the U.S. market and were still within their expiration date. Ceasing commercial distribution or expressing an intent to stop production did not retroactively relieve THM of its regulatory obligations, the FDA said. THM again refused to provide the requested records, according to the agency.
Meanwhile, CQT deregistered and discontinued its drug listing on June 29. The next day, the company told the FDA that it was unable to meet the agency’s requirements. CQT never provided the requested records. On July 13, CQT reregistered with the FDA.
On Aug. 26, the FDA issued import alerts for all drugs and drug products that CQT and THM offer to ship to the U.S. Officials generally detain imported drugs made by companies subject to import alerts. The policy of detaining imports without physical examination typically applies until the FDA completes an inspection.
The agency invited CQT and THM to schedule inspections. As of now, the FDA is unable to confirm the companies’ compliance with current good manufacturing practice (CGMP) and other applicable requirements, meaning it may withhold approval of new applications or supplements listing them as manufacturers.

source_document.body:
Every fleet manager knows the feeling of watching the pump price tick up and realizing there is nothing to be done about it. Diesel is set by forces no carrier controls. What a carrier does control is how much of every gallon it puts to work, and elevated fuel prices have a way of exposing habits that were quietly costing money all along. Idling that seemed tolerable at lower prices gets harder to ignore. So does a truck whose fuel economy has slipped unnoticed, or a driver whose habits show up in the fuel bill before they show up in a crash report.
“None of us can control the price at the pump,” said Josh Lovan, Industry Business Advisor at J. J. Keller & Associates, Inc. “What fleets can control is how efficiently they operate, how closely they monitor their costs and how quickly they respond when something doesn’t look right.”
That framing shifts the question. Instead of asking how a fleet absorbs a fuel spike, it asks which parts of the operation are leaking value, and whether anyone is positioned to catch it.
Start With the True Cost of a Mile
Cost control begins with knowing the real number and Lovan says the first step is understanding what higher fuel prices are doing to profitability.
“Understand your true cost per mile and how higher fuel prices are affecting profitability. Review your fuel surcharge programs regularly so they reflect changing fuel costs,” Lovan said. “Then use the telematics and fleet management systems you already have to find excessive idling, inefficient routing and unnecessary deadhead miles.”
Fuel economy tracking is the next layer. “Monitor MPG by vehicle,” Lovan said. “An unexplained decline could indicate a maintenance issue, inefficient operation or even fuel theft.”
That last risk is why he urges fleets to look closely at how fuel is purchased. “Review fuel card controls and transactions for unusual purchasing patterns or unauthorized use. And reinforce secure parking and fueling practices with drivers, because higher fuel prices make fuel theft more costly.”
Safety Is a Cost Control Strategy
Safety and fuel efficiency are often managed by different people against different goals, yet they are driven by many of the same behaviors.
“Some of the same behaviors we coach for safety, like controlling speed, avoiding aggressive driving and planning trips properly, can also help control operating costs,” Lovan said.
He points to specific behaviors and the tools that expose them. “Speeding, hard acceleration, hard braking and unnecessary idling are the ones to address through driver training and coaching. Telematics, dash cameras and driver scorecards show you which behaviors need attention. Use that fleet data to give targeted coaching instead of relying exclusively on broad annual training.”
The financial case extends well beyond fuel. “Reducing preventable crashes also reduces the costs that come with them, including repairs, downtime, towing and insurance exposure,” Lovan said. “And monitor roadside inspection and CSA data for recurring driver behaviors, because they can point to a larger training need.”
Good trip planning ties it together, helping drivers manage fueling, parking and hours of service safely and efficiently.
Maintenance Costs More When Fuel Costs More
Preventive maintenance is usually framed as a compliance obligation. When fuel is expensive, it is also a cost control measure. Tire pressure, condition and alignment all affect fuel efficiency as well as safety, so a small lapse in upkeep can add up across a fleet. Keeping preventive maintenance schedules matched to equipment and operating conditions keeps those lapses from compounding.
“A well maintained truck is not just more likely to pass an inspection,” Lovan said. “It is also more likely to perform the way the fleet expects it to.”
The details matter. “Maintain preventive maintenance schedules based on your equipment and operating conditions, and pay close attention to tire pressure, tire condition and alignment, because they affect fuel efficiency as well as safety,” Lovan said. “If you see an unexplained decline in fuel economy, investigate it. It could point to an underlying mechanical problem.”
He also cautions against measuring maintenance by the shop invoice alone. “The cost of maintenance includes more than repairs. Breakdowns can also mean towing, roadside service, missed deliveries and equipment downtime.”
Compliance Supports Profitability
Compliance rarely gets credit as a cost control tool, but its failures can take drivers and equipment out of service, interrupt operations and create administrative inefficiencies on top of citations and penalties.
“Good compliance makes the operation more predictable,” Lovan said. “When driver qualifications, hours of service, maintenance and vehicle records are managed correctly, you’re reducing the surprises that can take a truck or driver out of service.”
For Lovan, the foundation is accurate records and proactive monitoring. “Maintain accurate driver qualification files and have a system for monitoring expiring credentials and required documentation. Manage hours of service and ELD compliance proactively to minimize violations and improve trip planning,” he said. “Keep your vehicle inspection, repair and maintenance records current under 49 CFR Part 396, and keep IFTA mileage and fuel records accurate so applicable interstate vehicles are properly credentialed.”
Lovan adds that recurring problems tend to surface in the data first. “Monitor roadside inspection and CSA data to identify recurring compliance issues before they become bigger problems. For fleets managing a lot of moving parts, a centralized compliance platform that tracks driver, vehicle and regulatory requirements and alerts you to upcoming deadlines can help.”
Bring the Data Together
Fuel, safety, maintenance and compliance rarely operate in isolation. A drop in MPG can be a maintenance problem. A pattern of speeding can be both a coaching opportunity and a fuel problem. Managing each area separately makes those connections harder to see.
“Bring fuel, safety, maintenance and compliance data together instead of managing each area independently,” Lovan said. “Track a focused group of KPIs, such as MPG, fuel cost per mile, idle time, maintenance cost per mile, preventable crashes and downtime. Use the technology already available in your fleet to identify exceptions and trends that need attention.”
The harder part, he says, is follow-through. “Assign responsibility for acting on alerts and data. Technology provides little value if nobody responds to what it identifies. And if your fleet lacks the staff or resources to manage safety and compliance effectively, consider outside expertise.”
None of this requires a single sweeping cost-cutting initiative. The savings come from closing smaller inefficiencies consistently, and it works best as a standing approach rather than a reaction to a fuel spike.
“The goal isn’t just to burn less fuel. It’s to get more value out of every mile you’re already running,” Lovan said. “When safety, maintenance and compliance are working together, the fleet is generally going to be more efficient, more predictable and better positioned to handle whatever happens with fuel prices.”
Fuel prices will keep moving, and no fleet will ever control them. The operations that stay resilient treat the factors within their reach as a connected system and manage them that way.

By: Staff Writer November 11, 2026
Simandou’s rail and port operator aims to support 120 million tonnes of annual iron ore exports by the end of 2027, operations chief Matt Baartz said during a site visit Monday, according to Guinean news outlet Guinee360 .
The logistics network operated by Compagnie du TransGuinéen has annualized capacity of about 72 million tonnes, BMO Capital Markets said Wednesday, citing Bloomberg . Further expansion depends on deliveries of locomotives and wagons and commissioning the second stage of Morébaya port by March 2027, the bank said.
Mine output follows a separate schedule. Rio Tinto (ASX, LSE: RIO) said in October that its SimFer operation remained on track to reach an annual production rate of 60 million tonnes in the second half of 2028. SimFer accounts for half of Simandou’s planned mining capacity.
The pace of the increase will help determine how much competitive pressure Guinea places on established exporters. Simandou’s growing shipments are already offsetting supply declines elsewhere as weaker prices and higher freight and diesel costs squeeze producers, Macquarie Group analysts said in a note reported by Bloomberg on Nov. 3.
Shipments accelerate
Guinea exported 8.9 million tonnes of iron ore in the third quarter, 48% more than the 6 million tonnes shipped in the preceding three months, according to government data cited by Bloomberg . Baowu Winning Consortium Simandou accounted for 6.55 million tonnes and SimFer for 2.16 million tonnes.
Exports could reach about 28 million tonnes this year if October’s shipment pace holds and weather permits, Macquarie estimated. That forecast measures tonnes shipped over the year; the 120-million-tonne target describes the annual rate the infrastructure is intended to support.
Forecasts for reaching full output vary. Fearnley Securities projected 120 million tonnes of annual capacity during 2028, shipping publication TradeWinds reported in October. source_document.body:
The United States has extended the suspension of port fees targeting China-linked shipping for another two months, keeping the measures on hold through January 9, 2027, according to a notice published Tuesday in the Federal Register.
The decision gives Washington and Beijing additional time to negotiate over Chinese policies affecting the maritime, logistics and shipbuilding industries.
The Office of the United States Trade Representative said the extension took effect November 9 and runs through 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time on January 9. It follows a one-year suspension that began November 10, 2025, under a trade agreement announced by President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping.
The pause also continues to cover additional duties on Chinese ship-to-shore cranes and other cargo-handling equipment specified in the agency’s earlier action.
China also extended its suspension of reciprocal port fees on U.S.-linked vessels until January 10.
USTR said the circumstances supporting the original suspension remain in place and that further discussions with China are needed.
The U.S. fees could amount to millions of dollars for a single vessel’s visit. A 50,000-net ton ship, for example, would owe $2.5 million in charges.
The measures arose from the U.S. investigation under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974 into China’s targeting of the maritime, logistics and shipbuilding sectors for dominance. The suspended fee categories include charges affecting Chinese-owned or operated vessels, Chinese-built vessels and foreign-built vehicle carriers.
In comments to USTR, supporters of the pause argued that it would avoid higher shipping costs, prevent commercial disruptions and provide time for negotiations. Some sought permanent suspension of certain fees, warning that their return could disrupt trade and harm U.S. exports.
Opponents argued that the fees are needed to encourage investment in American shipbuilding and related industries, including container manufacturing. Some commenters also urged USTR to treat cargo-equipment tariffs separately from maritime service fees and end the suspension of those tariffs.
USTR said the United States will use the additional negotiating period to pursue its concerns with China while continuing efforts to expand domestic commercial shipbuilding capacity, develop the workforce and cooperate with allies.
Why it matters: The reciprocal pause averts additional shipping costs and potential disruptions affecting not only U.S. and Chinese carriers but also businesses worldwide that rely on Chinese-built vessels. It gives importers, exporters and shipowners temporary relief while trade negotiations continue.

Richard Petty's Daytona Boss 429 Powered This One-of-One 1970 Mustang Tasca Drag Racer, 3,000 Miles
85 photos
Photo: Bring A Trailer/HPHS81
"My father said, 'See that carbon on those pistons? That's Daytona carbon!' That Boss 429 was totally set up. I took Edsel Ford II for a ride one afternoon on the back roads. When I hit second gear the seat track broke and Edsel ended up in the back seat, but I just kept on going." Carl Tasca’s one-of-a-kind 1970 Ford Mustang Boss 429 drag race car would shut down everything else going on around it, no matter where it should happen to show up. And that’s saying something, since any Boss Nine, even the most run-of-the-mill example, is an event in itself.
First of all, allow me to express my deepest and most sincere sympathy for those who think the Ford Mustang Boss 429 is extraordinary, over-the-top, king of the hill, top of the heap, Big Boss. Well, truth be told, that last one isn’t exactly all that hyperbolizing of a descriptor, is it? I mean, it’s literally the car’s name. What more of an in-your-face sobriquet could it have? Well, here’s a suggestion, If I may "Petty Tasca."
Few names in American muscle car lore – particularly Blue Oval fan clubs – command the immediate reverence of Tasca Ford and Petty Enterprises. Virtually anything with ties to either of those two grand establishments will have gearheads listen, watch, and investigate with serious dedication.
Naturally, this one-off 1970 Ford Mustang Boss 429 currently up for grabs on Bring a Trailer unites both dynasties under one bulging fiberglass hood. And that’s not a metaphor – just scroll through the gallery and see the mountain hump laying claim over entire parcels of hood real estate.
Photo: Bring A Trailer/HPHS81 What separates this Grabber Blue fastback from the rest of the blue-chip collector pack is not untouched showroom originality, but a documented pedigree forged in factory-backed motorsport. Assigned Kar Kraft serial number 2124, Boss 429 #0F02Z109082 was delivered new to Bob Tasca’s famed dealership in East Providence, Rhode Island, where it was immediately drafted into straight-line combat rather than prepped for delivery to a wealthy high-octane addict.
Original factory paperwork confirms that this mean Mustang was invoiced on September 9, 1969, and cleared the Dearborn Assembly Plant Driveaway Garage on September 12, 1969, at 8:26 AM. Routed through Shelby and Kar Kraft under special order code DSO 89 2500, the Mustang was billed to Tasca Ford Sales at 777 Taunton Avenue in East Providence, Rhode Island, for $4,137.69.
If that seems suspiciously cheap , it is: the sticker price for retail customers was $5,107.95. However, Ford Division of Ford Motor Company invoiced the dealer at wholesale price, for obvious reasons. The wholesale bill gave Tasca Ford a gross paper margin of $970.26 – a 24% markup, if you care for bookkeeping.
Photo: Bring A Trailer/HPHS81 According to its Dearborn broadcast sheet, the nefarious pony car left the factory in Grabber Blue paint over White Corinthian vinyl high-back bucket seats. It carried the Drag Pack 3.91:1 rear axle, Competition Suspension, power front disc brakes, power steering, a console, a Rim-Blow steering wheel, an AM radio, the Decor and Convenience Check groups, an 8,000-rpm tachometer, a round clock, and a set of F60x15 raised-white-letter tires with no collapsible spare.
Few dealerships on earth could match the performance credentials of Tasca Ford, where patriarch Bob Tasca coined the motto "Win on Sunday, Sell on Monday" and fathered the 428-cubic-inch Cobra Jet. Period dealership records show Tasca sold seven 289 Shelby Cobras, six 427 Shelby Cobras, 162 Shelby Mustangs, 14 Boss 302s, six Boss 351s, seven 429 Super Cobra Jets, and nine Boss 429s, including this Grabber Blue 1970 fastback - Carl Tasca’s racer. Name no coincidence, in case you’re wondering.
Rather than racing the stock Z-code big-block V8 , Bob’s son and general manager, Carl Tasca, orchestrated a legendary engine swap. During the 1969 NASCAR season, Richard Petty briefly left Plymouth to campaign a Ford Torino Talladega in car number 43, winning nine races before returning to Mopar. As Carl Tasca recounted in the book “Boss Mustang: 50 Years” by Donald Farr, he acquired the Boss 429 V8 from Petty’s Daytona car.
Photo: Bring A Trailer/HPHS81 Carl Tasca vividly remembered driving to the Railway Express station in Lincoln, Rhode Island, to pick up the crated Petty Enterprises race motor for his second Boss 429, Kar Kraft 2124. Once back at the East Providence dealership, Tasca mechanics Bill Gilbert and John Healey pulled the aluminum cylinder heads off the block, prompting Bob Tasca to point at the pistons and exclaim that they still wore genuine Daytona carbon.
Keen-eyed gearheads will immediately raise an eyebrow, for good reason: Petty won the February 1969 Daytona 500 with a 427 V8 before the Boss 429 made its competition debut on March 31, 1969. The very first official NASCAR race featuring the legendary Boss 429 engine was the Atlanta 500 on March 30, 1969, held at the Atlanta Motor Speedway.
It was a dream debut for Ford's new powerplant, as it won the race on its very first outing. Cale Yarborough took the checkered flag driving a Mercury Cyclone prepped by the famous Wood Brothers racing team. Eventually, the Boss 429 race engine would sweep the season with 26 victories, bringing the 1969 championship cup over in Ford’s trophy room.
Photo: Bring A Trailer/HPHS81 Petty’s Talladega also raced the July 1969 Firecracker 400 at Daytona, and tested Boss 429 hardware extensively. It’s still a Daytona race, regardless of the exact date; Tasca Ford crowned Petty’s engine with a Weiand tunnel-ram intake, dual Holley four-barrel carburetors, and four-into-one headers.
Beneath the hand-cut hood scoop sat the 7.0-liter V8 featuring four-bolt main caps, forged steel internals, and aluminum cylinder heads with crescent-shaped combustion chambers and staggered valves. Basically, a semi-hemi, and the canted valves required oversized heads, leaving no room for anything else in the bay.
Fed by a single 735-cfm Holley four-barrel carburetor and breathing through a 10.5:1 compression ratio, the street engine was conservatively rated at 375 hp at 5,200 rpm and 450 lb-ft of torque at 3,400 rpm, though uncorked dynos revealed over 500 hp.
Photo: Bring A Trailer/HPHS81 Determined to dethrone Chrysler’s dominant 426 Hemi on NASCAR superspeedways, Ford developed a semi-hemispherical 429-cubic-inch V8, nicknamed the Blue Crescent. Because NASCAR rules mandated that at least 500 engines and host vehicles be sold to the public, Ford chose the Mustang to carry its new big-block weapon.
Produced across two model years, the Boss 429 saw 859 examples built for 1969 and 499 units completed for 1970, bringing the total run to 1,358 cars. Every single example left the line in the two-door SportsRoof fastback body style. Because the standard Mustang engine bay at Ford’s Dearborn assembly plant could not swallow the massive 429-cubic-inch block, unfinished cars were shipped to Kar Kraft in Brighton, Michigan.
Inside Kar Kraft’s facility at 800 Whitney Road, technicians hand-modified each Mustang by cutting and widening the front shock towers, beefing up the suspension with oversized spindles, and relocating the battery to the trunk. The resulting package carried a base price of $4,798 in 1969 and $4,918 in 1970, easily eclipsing the $5,000 mark with options and costing nearly double the price of a base Mustang SportsRoof fastback.
Photo: Bring A Trailer/HPHS81 The Boss 429 V8 alone was $1,208 retail price; Tasca was invoiced $955 for this Grabber Blue unit and its original motor. Every factory Boss 429 channeled its output through a close-ratio TopLoader four-speed manual transmission paired with a 3.91:1 Traction-Lok rear axle.
Choked by a small carburetor and saddled with street-biased Goodyear Polyglas GT tires, a stock example tested by Car Life in July 1969 sprinted from 0 to 60 mph in 7.1 seconds and cleared the standing quarter-mile in 14.09 seconds at 102.85 mph, begging for race-shop liberation. Which Tasca Ford had every intention of doing.
To clear the towering dual-quad induction setup, the dealership fabricated a domed lift-off hood secured by exposed pins, adding white hockey-stick stripes (you might have seen those on the other Boss Mustang of the period, the small-block 302 V8 “Son of Trans Am”), a white tail panel, gigantic traction bars, rear chassis reinforcements , a driveshaft safety loop, and 15-inch American Racing magnesium wheels.
Photo: Bring A Trailer/HPHS81 The setup hit so violently that when Carl Tasca took Edsel Ford II for a back-road ride and slammed second gear, the passenger seat, dumping Edsel into the back.
After Carl Tasca campaigned KK 2124 at northeastern drag strips and logged roughly 3,000 miles, the dealership retired the bruiser. A State of Connecticut tax form and sales paperwork from Tasca Lincoln-Mercury document the sale of the Mustang on September 30, 1974, to drag racer Henry E. Austin, Jr. for $4,500 cash, explicitly stipulating a race engine for race use only.
Operating out of Norwich, Connecticut, Henry E. Austin, Jr. raced the Petty-powered Mustang throughout the 1970s while carefully maintaining its Ford hardware . Invoices from Simon Ford in Norwich dated February 29, 1980, billed to Austin’s Amoco station, show him ordering a factory front spoiler, door weatherstrips, quarter-window moldings, and fuel tank components. An October 14, 1990, letter from registrar Steve Strange even referenced Austin’s vintage tractor-trailer race rig.
Photo: Bring A Trailer/HPHS81 Purchased by its current owner in 2014 after decades in storage, Kar Kraft 2124 underwent a exterior refinish in factory Grabber Blue by Randy DeLisio at DeLisio’s Performance in Lyons, New York, in 2015. Meanwhile, its Petty Enterprises NASCAR V8 was shipped to George’s Speed Shop in Dayton, Ohio, where International Drag Racing Hall of Fame legend "Ohio” George" Montgomery personally performed a $6,125 rebuild and dyno session.
Montgomery’s itemized invoice lists eight new pistons, connecting rods, a modified and balanced crankshaft, a roller-lifter camshaft, new valves, and oil restrictors to keep the Petty mill singing. Showing just 3,300 miles on its odometer and offered on a bill of sale with its original build sheet, factory invoice, and historical records, this one-of-one Tasca Petty Mustang Boss 429 is an irreplaceable monument to factory drag racing. It is also for sale.
The car is listed on Bring A Trailer, with the current bid standing at $150,500 (after less than 24 hours since the listing went live), and with six days left for prospects to place their bets. I know this is going to be high-dollar, but all I’m asking is your two cents’ worth in the comments: what’s this majestic unicorn’s correct price?

source_document.body:
Genesis opened orders for the ultra-luxury electric SUV in South Korea, with prices starting at over $100,000. If you want coach doors, however, it will cost you a bit more.
Genesis GV90 prices and driving range in Korea
Hyundai’s luxury brand is moving upscale with the GV90, its first fully electric three-row flagship SUV.
After unveiling the GV90 at the Palace of Fine Arts in San Francisco in August ( which we had the pleasure to see firsthand ), Genesis launched the new “ultra-luxe” SUV in its home market of Korea on Tuesday.
The Genesis GV90 introduces several “world-first” innovations, including the first independently opening and closing B-pillarless coach doors, a 12-airbag roof airbag system, and genuine wood floors with radiant heating.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
It’s available in two models: the GV90 Standard with traditional swing doors and the GV90 Neolun, which features the “Neolun Arch Gate,” Genesis’ hidden B-pillar coach door system.
In Korea, the Genesis GV90 Standard 7-seater model starts at 139.5 million won, or about $104,000.
Genesis GV90 Neolun (Source: Peter Johnson/ Electrek)
The GV90 Individual Lounge Seat (6-seater) starts at 145.5 million won ($108,500); the GV90 Neolun Standard (6-seater) starts at 189.9 million won ($141,500), while the top-spec GV90 Neolun Executive Suite (4-seater) starts at 239.5 million won ($178,500).
Based on Hyundai’s new eMP platform, developed exclusively for its flagships, Genesis said the GV90 is like a “moving private lounge,” complete with a multi-chamber air suspension and a dual electronic limited-slip differential (E-LSD).
Genesis GV90 Trim | Starting Price
GV90 Standard (7-seater) | 139.5 million won ($104,000)
GV90 Individual Lounge Seat (6-seater) | 145.5 million won ($108,500)
GV90 Neolun Standard (6-seater) | 189.9 million won ($141,500)
GV90 Neolun Executive Suite (4-seater) | 239.5 million won ($178,500)
Genesis GV90 price by trim in South Korea
A luxury private lounge on wheels
The platform is designed to open up interior space for the B-pillarless coach doors, swivel seats, and more.
When parked, the front seats swivel a full 180 degrees to face rear passengers or to create what Genesis calls “a face-to-face lounge-like configuration.”
The interior is about as over-the-top as you could expect, with massive digital screens, premium materials, and plenty of luxury extras.
The GV90 is the first Hyundai Motor Group vehicle to feature its new extendable display and the first Genesis model equipped with its next-gen Pleos Connect infotainment system.
Together, they create what Genesis calls a new realm of “display expandability.” While other vehicles, like the new Tucson and IONIQ 3, also use Pleos Connect, Hyundai developed an exclusive version for the GV90.
Genesis GV90 Neolun infotainment display (Source: Peter Johnson/ Electrek)
When the vehicle is parked, the screen can expand to 24.6″ at the push of a button, transforming it into a massive Cinematic Display.
Once extended, the display switches to Media Home mode, where you can watch Netflix, live TV, stream music, and more with third-party apps.
A mobile private theater wouldn’t be complete without a premium audio system, right? To top it off, Genesis added a 25-speaker Bang & Olufsen Premier 3D Sound System with Dolby Atmos, so it sounds like you’re actually at the movies.
In place of a traditional instrument cluster, the GV90 has a 25″ Head-Up Display (HUD) that shows the vehicle’s speed, navigation directions, and other ADAS functions directly on the windshield.
The GV90 is also the first Hyundai Motor Group vehicle with a buttonless power system. When you enter the vehicle and close the door, the Motion Column Shifter moves from the 12 o’clock position to the 2 o’clock position.
Meanwhile, the Crystal Sphere between the driver and passenger rotates to indicate it’s ready to drive. The vehicle starts when you press the brake.
Genesis GV90 debut (Source: Peter Johnson/ Electrek)
Dimensions, battery size, other specs
As a full-size flagship SUV, the Genesis GV90 is massive. It measures 208.1″ (5,285 mm) long, 79.9″ (2,030 mm) wide, and 71.5″ (1,815 mm) tall (71.4″ with 24″ tires), with a 127.8″ (3,245 mm) wheelbase.
That’s even bigger than the Hyundai IONIQ 9 (199.2″/5,060 mm in length) and Kia EV9 (197.4″/5,010 mm).
To power a full-size flagship SUV, it needs a big battery. The GV90 uses a 123.5 kWh battery, the largest among Hyundai Motor’s EVs, which Genesis said provides a driving range of 500 km (310 miles) for the 7-seater version with 22″ wheels.
The GV90 Neonlun 6-seater with 24″ wheels has a range of up to 460 km (286 miles) on a single charge.
It’s equipped with a new dual-motor all-wheel-drive (AWD) system that delivers a combined 657 hp (490 kW) and 590 lb-ft (800 Nm) of torque, making it Hyundai Motor Group’s most powerful electric vehicle.
When using a 350 kW fast charger, the vehicle’s battery can recharge from 10% to 80% in about 22 minutes.
Genesis GV90 Neolun (left) GV90 Neolun First Edition (middle) and GV90 (right) Source: Hyundai
“Thanks to the enthusiastic interest and support for the GV90 since its global premiere, we have begun full-scale sales in Korea first,” a Genesis official said, adding the flagship SUV will “set a new standard for luxury.”
Following Korea, Genesis is expected to launch the GV90 in the US and other global markets in early 2027.
Genesis has yet to reveal US prices, but the GV90 Standard model is expected to start at around $100,000. The GV90 Neolun, on the other hand, will likely start closer to $150,000 or more.
What do you think of the flagship Genesis GV90? Would you buy the standard version for about $100,000 or pay the extra for the Neolun with coach doors? Let us know in the comments.

Toyota and Subaru’s new electric SUVs are catching on with buyers, offering various options and prices ranging from about $35,000 to $45,000, or the “sweet spot” of the US market.
Toyota and Subaru EVs catch on at affordable prices
The US electric vehicle market rebounded in the third quarter with 262,649 EVs sold, according to Kelley Blue Book estimates, up 6.1% from Q2 and the strongest performance of the year.
Although nearly every automaker has sold fewer EVs so far this year than in the same period in 2025, as buyers rushed to claim the $7,500 tax credit before it expired, a handful of brands are seeing considerably higher demand.
Outside of Rivian, Toyota and Subaru are the only brands that have higher year-over-year EV sales in the US through the third quarter.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
Combined, Toyota and Subaru have sold nearly 50,000 EVs through the first nine months of 2026, more than double compared to the same period last year.
Toyota alone has sold nearly 35,000 electric vehicles, up 183.4% YOY, while Subaru sold 14,630, up 46.7%. And that’s not even including the additional 12,676 sold under the Lexus brand, up 137.4% YOY.
2027 Toyota bZ (Source: Toyota)
While the two Japanese automakers were infamously slow to transition to battery electric vehicles, the timing worked in their favor.
After launching the heavily updated bZ in late 2025, previously called the bZ4X, Toyota’s electric SUV suddenly became one of America’s most popular EVs. Through Q3, it was the fourth best-selling EV in the US , trailing only the Hyundai IONIQ 5, Tesla Model 3, and Tesla Model Y.
Toyota bZ interior (Source: Toyota)
Starting at $35,000, the Toyota bZ is one of the most affordable EVs in the US. It also offers up to 314 miles of range in the FWD Plus trim, which starts at $37,980.
Toyota and Subaru now each sell three electric SUVs , which share the same platform and technology.
From left to right: Toyota C-HR, bZ, and bZ Woodland electric SUVs (Source: Toyota)
With prices ranging from roughly $35,000 to about $45,000, Stephanie Valdez Streaty, director of industry insights at Cox Automotive , said (via Bloomberg ) Toyota and Subaru’s new EVs are affordable and hit the “sweet spot” of the US car market.
Toyota also sells the smaller, sporty C-HR, starting at $37,080, and the larger, more rugged bZ Woodland, which starts at $45,380.
2027 Subaru Uncharted EV (Source: Subaru)
Subaru, on the other hand, sells the updated Solterra ($38,495, plus the smaller Uncharted ($34,995) and midsize Trailseeker ($39,995).
Karla Fisher, a Marine and retired engineer, told Bloomberg that the Subaru Trailseeker was her “most favorite car of all time.”
While she considered buying an EV before the $7,500 federal credit expired last September, none met her requirements at the time. Fisher wanted at least 7″ of ground clearance, 250 miles or more range, and a price that was similar, or even less than a comparible gas-powered vehicle.
Subaru Trailseeker (Source: Subaru)
The Subaru Trailseeker offers all of that and starts at under $40,000. Toyota and Subaru’s electric SUVs all start at about $45,000 or less, which is even less than the average new vehicle.
According to the latest Kelley Blue Book figures, the average price for a new vehicle in the US reached a record $51,109 in October, up 2.1% YOY.

BMW Adds South Korea's Samsung SDI and LG Energy Solution to Gen6 High-Voltage Battery Supply Chain
12 photos
Photo: BMW
BMW has recently confirmed that Samsung SDI and LG Energy Solution will become integral parts of the Munich-based automaker's electric vehicle supply chain. The South Korean companies will supply cells for sixth-generation batteries from regional facilities, beginning in the latter part of the 2020s.
The question is, why? Doesn't BMW have sufficient high-voltage battery cell suppliers to satisfy demand? The move is a little more complex, though. Simply put, BMW has expanded its battery cell supplier portfolio while bringing a new layer of regional sourcing to its growing electric vehicle production network.
By contracting the folks at Samsung and LG, the German automaker isn't abandoning existing partners or Chinese suppliers. Instead, the manufacturer wants more options in the regions where it builds electric vehicles. This way, it reduces exposure to individual supplier-level issues and long-distance logistics.
BMW will continue sourcing Euro-produced cells from Chinese heavyweights CATL and EVE Energy, with Samsung SDI joining that supplier group for good measure. LG Energy Solution, meanwhile, will become another supplier for the automaker's North American operations. BMW even has a name for this particular strategy, calling it "local for local" in the attached media release.
In addition to selecting a battery supplier with a factory somewhere on the same continent, the L4L philosophy also means that battery cells will travel shorter distances between their production facilities, the plants where they morph into high-voltage battery assemblies, and vehicle assembly plants. An efficiently coordinated manufacturing network, if you will.
Photo: BMW The agreements with Samsung and LG concern Gen6 battery cells, which define the Neue Klasse-based i3 and iX3 lines. Gen6 technologies have also carried over to Cluster Architecture-based electric models . Samsung SDI will supply these large-format cylindrical cells, which are completely different in design from the fifth-generation rectangular prismatic cells, to European facilities.
LG, on the other hand, will support North American operations. The Spartanburg facility in the United States of America comes to mind, while BMW Group Plant San Luis Potosi in Mexico prepares for volume production of electric vehicles in 2027. The Mexican plant has received 800 million euros to prepare for Neue Klasse vehicle production, which includes the iX3 and i3.
Chinese battery cell suppliers remain important for BMW, yet choosing Samsung and LG for Europe and North America further demonstrates that BMW is reducing its dependence on CATL and EVE. It's only natural to do so, considering the Asian country's dominant position in cell manufacturing and the processing of battery materials.
Think about the consequences of battery diplomacy for Europe and North America for a minute. Not even political leaders are okay with China's dominance in this domain, let alone car manufacturers that are mostly dependent on Chinese battery cell suppliers. Looking at the bigger picture, what BMW did here was to reduce the risk that a disruption, be it a geopolitical situation or simply an individual supplier-level problem, will interfere with electric vehicle production.

The Hunter Nature NTR 4XL Travel Trailer Is Beefy, Compact, and Absolutely Packed
28 photos
Photo: Hunter Nature
What is more or less a common sight in the U.S. is… not so much on the European caravan scene. Beefy, utilitarian offroad travel trailers remain the exception, not the rule, here, but that's not what makes a unit like the NTR 4XL a standout.
This is one of the newest creations from Turkish company Hunter Nature, which previously made headlines for the Raptor offroad expandable trailer, which was actually a more evolved version of the original Campravan Raptor XC . Neither is still in production, with the company replacing them with the five-entry NTR series.
The NTR4X, which is now being sold as NTR 4XL in the UK by partner Pilgrim Caravans Outdoors and which you can see in the video tour at the bottom of the page, is the second largest entry in this series. NTR obviously stands for "nature" because this trailer takes you out into nature and lets you stay there for as long as you can manage resources.
While the aesthetics of the NTR 4XL are similar to the newer trailers from Camppass , which are also designed and produced in Turkey, Hunter Nature claims to have been one of the pioneers, if not actually the first manufacturer of truly offroad caravans in Europe. The company has been on the market since 1987, but only offered components and parts until 2019, when they started building their own units.
Photo: Hunter Nature/Pilgrim Caravans Outdoors They imagined those as European-compliant in every way, but with an edge over every other manufacturer in that they would be truly offroad units.
All this explains the beastly, utilitary, almost military-inspired aesthetic of the NTR 4XL. This is an offroad caravan, but at the same time, it's a unit that can offer accommodation to the entire family and cover the basic needs. It offers comfort throughout the year, and it does so with certain flair. It's not an elegant caravan in the strictest sense of the word, but that's not to say that it's not good looking.
The NTR 4XL is built on a steel chassis with a full aluminum body . It comes standard with KNOTT brakes, a single axle with independent spring suspension, and a pop-up roof with canvas sections. The pop-up roof system was designed specifically for Hunter Nature and it can be operated with a single hand thanks to pneumatic pistons and scissor mechanism.
Photo: Hunter Nature/Pilgrim Caravans Outdoors The pop-up roof adds 45 cm extra inside, so you get full standing height, but the trailer remains functional even with it closed. The manufacturer says that this allows for year-round use and even comfortable use in extreme temperatures: you pop the roof for extra ventilation in hot weather and hunker down with it closed in freezing temps.
Speaking of extreme weather, the NTR 4XL is fully insulated. However, a space heater is only offered as an optional extra, though it will be an actual necessity if you're planning adventures in the wintertime.
This floorplan comes in at 3.7 meters/12.1 feet of length in the body (5.1 meters/16.7 feet overall), 2.58 meters/8.4 feet of overall height with the roof closed, and 2.22 meters/7.2 feet in width. It's a compact towable even by European standards, which makes the high sleeping capacity it offers even more impressive.
Photo: Hunter Nature/Pilgrim Caravans Outdoors The British version (NTR 4XL) is described as a four-person caravan , but the original one (NTR4X) is actually rated for six people if you attach a double bed to the roof. The layout is the same for both versions, with a U-shaped dinette at the rear that converts into a double bed by dropping the table and two kids' bunks at the front.
In between these two, you get a compact galley kitchen on the campside, complete with a two-burner and sink combo, a sink, some prep space, and all-aluminum cabinetry. A nice fridge with freezer is available across the way, together with more (aluminum) cabinetry.
The bathroom is tucked between the bunks and the fridge, and it seems to be finished off in aluminum and fiberglass. It's a wet one, as you should have expected given the dimensions of the trailer, equipped with a slim vanity with a faucet, a separate shower, and an optional cassette toilet.
Photo: Hunter Nature/Pilgrim Caravans Outdoors Standard features include 410W of solar on the roof, a 200 or a 300Ah battery, AL-KO stabilizers, and electrostatic paint in military green or light gray. Not listed but shown in photos and the video below is an electric step and what looks like a large storage box on the front of the trailer.
The trailer can hold 140 liters (37 gallons) of freshwater and 75 liters (20 gallons) of gray. It doesn't have a black tank because you get the cassette toilet.
Options include the space heater, an outdoor shower complete with a shower curtain, an outdoor kitchen, and an e-mover that will help with parking.
Photo: Hunter Nature/Pilgrim Caravans Outdoors Empty weight of the NTR 4XL is at around 1,400-1,600 kg (3,086-3,527 lbs), while maximum permissible weight is 2,500 kg (5,511 lbs), so you can take plenty of stuff with you.
Neither Hunter Nature nor the British distributor offer prices , so you have to contact them for a quote if you like what you see.
Photo: Hunter Nature/Pilgrim Caravans Outdoors However, the description of the video below drops the £55,560 figure, which I take is for the complete unit shown, which also has the outdoor shower. That's approximately €66,500 or $73,800 at the current exchange rate, and above average pricing for a European caravan.
